chunks: As for what was narrated by Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn, from Fadalah, from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from Abi Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

I led my companions in the maghrib prayer, and when I had prayed two rak'ahs, I gave salām. Then some of them said: You only prayed two rak'ahs. So I repeated it. Then I informed Abā 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام, and he said: “Perhaps you repeated it.”

I said: Yes. So he laughed, then said: “It would only have sufficed you to stand and perform one rak'ah. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forgot and gave salām after two rak'ahs; then he mentioned the hadith of Dhu al-Shimalayn and said: then he stood and added two rak'ahs to it.”

key_terms.حَدِيثَ ذِي الشِّمَالَيْنِ: the report concerning Dhu al-Shimalayn about forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.سَلَّمْتُ: I gave the salām ending the prayer
key_terms.سَهَا: forgot or erred unintentionally in prayer
key_terms.يُجْزِيكَ: it would have been sufficient for you

ai.seo_question: If someone gives salām after two rak'ahs in maghrib prayer by mistake, must the whole prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of forgetting part of the prayer and ending the maghrib prayer after only two rak'ahs. Imam Abū 'Abd Allāh عليه السلام explains that repeating the whole prayer was unnecessary, and that completing the missing rak'ah would have sufficed. He supports this by citing an incident involving the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
